newsitem.title: USA: Mo. Supreme Court overturns Branson tourism tax.
newsitem.headline: Mo. Supreme Court overturns Branson tourism tax.

text.p: Missouri Supreme Court justices have overturned a state tourism tax that backs up to $46 million of debt for Branson drinking water and wastewater treatment plants as unconstitutional special legislation, spokesmen for the city and Gov. Mel Carnahan said Thursday.

Branson city officials created a reserve fund when the tax challenge lawsuit was filed in the event of an adverse ruling, leaving no immediate impact on debt service payments, city spokesman Jerry Adams said.

Branson's city administrator, mayor, bond counsel and community leaders met with Carnahan on Wednesday to discuss what could be "a significant problem" for the city, Carnahan's spokesman Chris Sifford said.

"Clearly this is a significant part of our economy," Sifford said. "Branson is a tremendous asset to the State of Missouri and we want to make sure it continues to grow and prosper so we will be looking at options out there."
One option would be a special session, Sifford said. Lawmakers are scheduled to meet for a veto session in September and could hold a special session at that time to address the ruling, he said.

By applying only to a city in a county bordering Arkansas, the tourism tax "is a facially special law, and its unconstitutionality is presumed," the state supreme court ruled Tuesday, overturning a Taney County judge's decision.

"Since the city has not met its burden of demonstrating substantial justification for the geographical classification, that presumption has not been overcome," Judge Ronnie White wrote in the four-page decision.
The tourism tax instituted in 1993 places a 4 percent levy on lodging and tickets and a 1 percent tax on restaurant bills, Adams said.

The tax applied only to a municipality with 3,000 to 5,000 residents, more than 5,000 hotel and motel rooms within city limits, and located in a county bordering on Arkansas, the supreme court decision stated.
